groups.name: Common Data Model

objectives.objective: Release OMOP CDM v5.5 using a focused, community-validated, time-bounded process.
krs: KR1 (Q1-Q2 2026): documented feedback on each v5.5 proposal from relevant WGs, the Technical Advisory Board and core tool/method maintainers.
KR2 (mid-2026): turn feedback into explicit go / modify / defer decisions for each proposal.
KR3: ship a CDM v5.5 candidate release and get Steering Committee approval, with updated DDLs, docs, R package, migration testing and a summary of community feedback.

notes: Aims to ship v5.5 around the August 2026 vocabulary release.
CDM WG liaisons contact other WGs for feedback; the timeline may slip because of the Teams outage.

groups.name: Data Quality

objectives.objective: Mature the Data Quality Dashboard with a community-driven roadmap aligned with current tooling.
krs: KR1: publish DQD on CRAN.
KR2: complete and publish a landscape assessment of data quality approaches used across OHDSI (tools, workflows, dimensions), with overlaps, gaps and unmet needs.
KR3: community-informed proposal for improving DQD reporting structures, including 1-2 feasible high-impact enhancements.

notes: KR1 was already done by the call: the Data Quality Dashboard is on CRAN.
The WG was on hiatus in 2025 while the CDM team focused on v5.5 proposals.
Asks other WGs for data quality checks to ship with their conventions (e.g. eye care visual acuity).

groups.name: OHDSI Evidence Network

objectives.objective: Professionalize and scale the Evidence Network
krs: Launch the Evidence Network website (partner onboarding, documentation, study tracking).
Publish a Data Partner Onboarding Playbook and governance templates.
Develop leadership- and industry-facing pitch materials.
Define sustainable funding pathways (grants, industry collaboration).

objectives.objective: Standardize the Evidence Network study lifecycle
krs: Define an end-to-end lifecycle (idea, feasibility, execution, synthesis).
Publish role definitions (Study Lead, Data Partner Lead, Local PI, Coordinating Center).
Release a Study Starter Kit (protocol and communications templates, governance checklist).
Improve visibility into active studies and partner participation.

objectives.objective: Enable reliable federated study execution
krs: Establish standardized execution and QA/QC workflows.
Define expectations for reruns, validation and issue resolution.
Provide clear results-submission guidance.
Iteratively refine guidance from real network studies.

notes: Run as workstreams: website, study lifecycle (with CHOP) and data partner engagement.
Open to anyone; you do not need to be a data partner.

groups.name: Eye Care and Vision Research

objectives.objective: Promote eye-focused standards within and outside OMOP
krs: Finalize ETL conventions for best recorded visual acuity (including pediatrics).
Formalize conventions in THEMIS.
Work with sites to execute the script.
Publish experience and promote the standards.

objectives.objective: Complete a network study with eye exam elements
krs: Glaucoma prediction study.
Design another network study with eye exam data.
Brainstorm a LEGEND for ophthalmology.

objectives.objective: Expand ophthalmic imaging capacity
krs: Demonstrate ophthalmic imaging integration using AI-READi data.
Develop a cross-cutting clinical informatics / imaging informatics curriculum.

objectives.objective: Integrate with other working groups (GIS, Medical Imaging, Patient-Level Prediction)
Disseminate work
krs: Publish WG activities.
Educate the community.
Collaborate with other ophthalmic standards groups.

notes: Intraocular pressure conventions are done; the best recorded visual acuity ETL is being tested, with recommendations going to LOINC.
Glaucoma prediction study is kicking off; imaging work links to the NIH-funded AI-READI project.
The American Academy of Ophthalmology asked for a regular check-in.
The WG is organized into subgroups that work asynchronously.

groups.name: Psychiatry

objectives.objective: Expand clinical vocabulary for psychiatric assessments
krs: Classify what each instrument is used for (which diagnosis).
Create a list of entities and relationships to adapt into the survey model.

objectives.objective: Run studies that show the need for the expanded assessment vocabulary
krs: Distribution of completed psychiatric assessments across patients with a defined diagnosis in a federated OMOP network (diagnoses to be defined).
Correlation between clinical outcomes for selected diagnosis categories and assessment scores (diagnoses to be defined).

objectives.objective: Grow engagement
krs: Run a workshop in the psychiatric research space to increase engagement with OMOP.
Build out the Psychiatry GitHub website and WG structure.

notes: Looking for psychiatrists, psychologists and therapists to help map assessments, and for sites with psychometric data (claims data usually lacks it).

groups.name: HADES

objectives.objective: Support the design of studies using HADES/Strategus with GenAI
krs: Identify package gaps that block GenAI-assisted study design.
Expand code examples for characterization, estimation and prediction designs, for humans and GenAI.
Provide an end-to-end example from study inception to results that uses GenAI.
Compare vibe coding with Strategus against using HADES packages directly.

objectives.objective: Mature HADES packages and workflows
krs: All HADES packages tested across all supported database platforms.
Support OHDSI-recommended study design and results-review workflows.
Study results reviewable through a DuckDB backend (only Postgres supported now).

objectives.objective: Add support for CDM extensions
krs: Define how HADES is extended (FeatureExtraction + Circe).
Support n "official" extensions.

notes: Gaps in the packages come from both user experience and the team's own GenAI experiments; file GitHub issues for problems.
The number of official CDM extensions is a placeholder until the work evolves.

groups.name: Medical Imaging
groups.meets: Every two weeks, alternating 7 am and 7 pm

objectives.objective: Dissemination and education (priorities: Must Have / Intend to Have / Like to Have)
krs: Must Have: Book of OHDSI imaging chapter.
Must Have: GitHub instructions.
Must Have: ETL conventions web page.
Must Have: training workshop for implementing the extension.
Intend to Have: DICOM/RadLex non-standard semantics into the OHDSI Vocabulary (with Vocabulary WG).
Intend to Have: DICOM Waveform, ECG to DICOM (with Waveform WG).

objectives.objective: Imaging research and adoption
krs: Like to Have: first imaging network study.
Like to Have: first multi-modal network study.
Like to Have: 10 sites implementing the MI extension.
Like to Have: paper on feasibility of the MI-CDM in dentistry (with Dentistry WG).

notes: Three sites already run the imaging extension; the stretch goal is 10.
Three papers published and two in press (high-value DICOM tags; FAIR imaging research with OMOP).
A hands-on workshop for the Symposium has been proposed.

groups.name: Education

objectives.objective: 2026 OKRs (objectives not labelled on the slide)
krs: Publish the 2nd edition of the Book of OHDSI.
Create a consortium of colleges and universities teaching OHDSI in the classroom.
Create a public catalog of OHDSI educational programs (annual workshops and programs; Columbia and Oxford).
Build a searchable, self-maintaining repository of OHDSI educational artifacts (GitHub, PubMed, YouTube) with a community dashboard.
Identify learning pathways and develop resources to support them.
Organize leadership summits for OHDSI WG leads.
Create a leadership development training program template for clinical working groups.

notes: Five universities are already interested in teaching OHDSI.
The community dashboard was re-engineered: it classifies publications as OHDSI-related and indexes GitHub and YouTube artifacts.
The leadership program template comes from the maternal health fellowship.

groups.name: Health Systems Interest Group

objectives.objective: Support transforming source EHR data to the OMOP CDM
krs: Host 6 office-hours HSIG meetings a year (first Monday of the month, starting March 2).
Monitor and respond to forum questions (CDM Builders, Implementers, Uncategorized).
Provide practical guidance on source data mapping and ETL challenges.

objectives.objective: Strengthen HSIG contributions to OHDSI knowledge
krs: Feed health-system use cases and lessons learned into the Book of OHDSI.

objectives.objective: Improve HSIG visibility and usability
krs: Reorganize and update the HSIG webpage.
Make resources easier to find for new and existing members.

notes: An interest group, not a working group; a new co-lead joined on the call.

groups.name: OHDSI APAC

objectives.objective: Make APAC more researchable (one-sentence goal for 2026), across research, training and communication pillars
krs: Research: conduct one simple study that as many partners as possible can join (basic characterization or treatment pathway); breadth over depth. Lesson from 2025: supporting three China network studies at once was too many.
Training: finalize the curriculum being built with NUS (virtual summer course, now established) and the AIDEN nationwide OMOP adoption initiative.
Communication: keep community calls, newsletters and forums to link East and West; support new chapters (Indonesia filed, Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam in the pipeline).
APAC Symposium 2026 in Seoul, Korea (date to be confirmed; "sometime in November").

notes: Last year: three China network studies were too many at once; the Singapore GLP-1 study was being expanded; the Book of OHDSI was translated into Japanese.

groups.name: Vocabulary

objectives.objective: Support vocabulary-related activities of workgroups and contributors
krs: Hold regular office hours for vocabulary users and contributors.
With the Survey WG, develop and publish guidelines for survey, stage and scale, and patient-reported outcomes harmonization.

objectives.objective: Increase vocabulary content and process transparency
krs: Run sessions on all proposed changes and improvements (community contributions and roadmap).
Publish guidelines on mapping rules and assumptions for conditions, measurements, procedures and drugs.

objectives.objective: Enable vocabulary-related collaboration in the community
krs: With the GenAI WG, host a vocabulary mapping challenge at the OHDSI EU Symposium.

notes: Office hours resume in March (new link on the ohdsi.org page).
Conditions mapping guidelines are live and will be shared for comment; drugs are next.
The challenge answers many people independently working on LLM-assisted mapping.

groups.name: FHIR to OMOP

objectives.objective: Advance the HL7 Vulcan FHIR-to-OMOP implementation guide from balloted informative to STU (Standard for Trial Use) in the September 2026 HL7 ballot window
Deepen ties between the OHDSI and HL7 communities through the Vulcan FHIR Accelerator and joint initiatives
Improve OHDSI community engagement and drive adoption of the specification and tooling
krs: Show up at WG meetings, community calls and symposium presentations.

notes: The HL7 Vulcan FHIR Accelerator meets weekly and balloted the implementation guide last year.

groups.name: Rare Diseases

objectives.objective: Community engagement and collaboration
krs: Keep the collaborative team of about 20 active members.
Organize monthly sessions.
Establish partnerships with researchers, clinicians, patient advocacy groups, regulators and industry.

objectives.objective: Explore scalable rare disease analytics
krs: Design and start a multi-site rare disease study on the OHDSI network and OMOP CDM.
Develop an approach for identifying and integrating hard-to-find rare disease cohorts across sources (structured data standardization, deep clinical granularity).
Release preliminary findings and methodological insights.

notes: Two panels are planned (rare disease evidence with pharma, academia and the FDA; evidence submission).
One or two real-world drug development use cases across US and EU sites, using clinical notes (about 95% of rare disease information sits only in notes).

groups.name: Surgery and Perioperative Medicine

objectives.objective: Data, vocabulary and standards
krs: Review 10K codes for the ICD10PCS to SNOMED update (Aug 2026 edition), via LLM methods and manual review.
Abstract on procedure mapping issues and progress (Global Symposium).
Further discussion of CPT pending.

objectives.objective: Guideline-driven evidence generation and dissemination
krs: Complete "How Often Events Unfold in Surgery"; publish HORUS-AKI and at least one other HORUS study.
Publish one surgery cohort phenotype description.

objectives.objective: Evidence consumer engagement
krs: Present at at least 3 surgery / anesthesia / perioperative conferences.
Involve at least 3 new members from 3 surgery / perioperative lab groups.

objectives.objective: OHDSI community collaboration
krs: Two strategic collaborations with other WGs (Device, Waveform, Patient-Level Prediction, Oncology), with 2 joint meetings in 2026.

notes: HORUS is the surgery counterpart to How Often: large-scale incidence rates, first study on AKI.
Looking for ETL expertise on the device table and surgeries.

groups.name: Natural Language Processing

objectives.objective: Multi-site clinical studies using both structured and textual data
krs: MDD to bipolar diagnostic transition predictors, retrospective network study with Psychiatry: model development.
SDoH and treatment outcomes in type 2 diabetes (LEGEND-T2DM): multi-site validation of existing SDoH NLP pipelines.

objectives.objective: Open-source LLMs for information extraction from clinical notes
krs: Publish and open-source several information extraction pipelines.
Design a new AI agent-based tool for information extraction.

objectives.objective: Knowledge dissemination
krs: Monthly presentations on NLP advances (9 in 2025, about 30 attendees on average).

notes: Older packages are poorly maintained; focus is moving to LLM and agent-based extraction (e.g. Yale's KIWI, adapted to output OMOP concept IDs).
Considering a lessons-learned guide for LLM-based NLP in real-world studies (not committed).

groups.name: Latin America Chapter

objectives.objective: Strengthen OMOP adoption initiatives in LATAM
krs: At least 100 people at the first OHDSI Latin America Symposium.
At least 10 institutions engaged in the chapter.
At least 5 LATAM countries represented.
Activities: host the first Latin America Symposium, active chapter participation, one round of collective vocabulary mapping.

notes: 2025 lesson: activities that did not match the region's maturity did not engage people, hence the regional vocabulary mapping round.

groups.name: Oncology

objectives.objective: Enable observational cancer research. Pillar: community support and collaboration
krs: Update the Oncology wiki with onramps for ETLers and researchers.

objectives.objective: Pillar: high-quality oncology OHDSI data network
krs: Data partner certification.
Continuous improvement of oncology data readiness.
Genomic vocabulary update.
Targeted, use-case-driven vocabulary update.

objectives.objective: Pillar: evidence generation
krs: Guideline-driven evidence generation, finalizing FALCON-Bladder.
Regular use-case repo updates.

notes: The ETL on-ramp was already available for review by the end of February.
FALCON-Bladder has 65 data partners interested.
Subgroups: vocabulary and development, genomics/omics, outreach and research.

groups.name: Health Equity

objectives.objective: Research, one population-level characterization study
krs: Define and launch one health equity characterization study on OMOP with the GIS WG, characterizing disparities using place-based and/or SDoH variables across at least one OHDSI network site.

objectives.objective: Engagement, at least 2 external (non-OHDSI) speakers
krs: Invite public health, social epidemiology and community health researchers to WG sessions.

objectives.objective: Integration, map the Health Equity x GIS shared SDoH landscape
krs: Identify overlap between place-based SDoH data needs and OHDSI geospatial infrastructure; co-define at least one operational SDoH variable for OMOP (e.g. Area Deprivation Index).

notes: Was on hiatus late 2025; 2025 OKRs were too broad, so 2026 is deliberately narrow.
First meeting of the year: third week of March.

groups.name: Early-Stage Researchers

objectives.objective: Foster mentorship and engagement with more experienced researchers
krs: Monthly online and annual in-person Meet-the-Mentor roundtables and talks.

objectives.objective: Facilitate involvement, visibility and networking for ESRs
krs: At least 5 ESR presentations or posters at OHDSI symposia.
Spotlight ESR members' in-progress research at monthly meetings.

objectives.objective: Expand the leadership structure and support global participation
krs: Identify representatives to liaise with regional chapters.
Expand membership to include active members from at least three regional chapters.

notes: Meet-the-Mentor runs in the second half of WG calls.
A Symposium showcase checkbox and a separate ESR award exist.
